newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO INVITE POWER PLANT TENDERS IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO INVITE POWER PLANT TENDERS IN JULY.

text.p: Hungary's electricity supplier MVM said on Monday RWE 's plan to build two new 500 megawatt plants in Hungary was part of MVM's plans in July to invite bids for 2000 megawatts of new Hungarian capacity.

"There will be two closed tenders for 1,000 MW each, the first for smaller units and the second for larger plants which have a longer lead-in time," MVM's strategic director Istvan Bakacs told Reuters.

The tender for smaller capacity plants of 20 to 200 MW will be for commissioning beween 2001 and 2003 while the second tender will be for larger units to go on line between 2003 and 2005, Bakacs said.
Bakacs said the siting of the new plants will be for the bidders to suggest but acknowledged that RWE had already said it would bid in the second of the two tenders.
German consortium RWE Energie AG and EVS AG announced plans on Monday to build two new 500 MW power plants at Matra power plant site it runs in north east Hungary.
The company said it would put in a bid provided current drawn-out talks on energy pricing were resolved.

Bakacs said it was likely that the two July tenders would include a clause saying that no one constructor would be able to own and operate more than 30 percent of Hungary's total capacity, which currently stands at 7,500 MW.
"Even of RWE wins the tender for two 500 MW units, with the other 800 MW it already operates it will still be inside the limit," he said.

Bakacs added that MVM will publish the invitation to tender in mid-July and the preliminary bids should be received by mid-September. This will be follwed by a negotiation stage of five months, with the whole process expected to take around nine months.

The Matra investment programme represents one of the biggest foreign investments RWE has been involved in and the largest such programme in any of the ten countries applying to join the European Union (EU), the company said earlier.

Earlier on Monday, British generator Powergen Plc said it had secured a long-term power purchase agreement in Hungary, paving the way for the development of a 160 million pound ($261 million) power plant in Budapest.
